evidence: src/rebar/audit/server.py:101: `if rebar.error_code_for(exc) != "store_uninitialized": raise` — the consumer discriminates on the code, not the message
CHANGELOG.md:27: 'New error code `store_uninitialized` ... so the fault above is machine-readable over the MCP envelope rather than requiring message-text matching'

tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py:91: `assert _NOT_INITIALIZED in str(excinfo.value)` — the only assertion; `_NOT_INITIALIZED = "not initialized"` (line 55). No `error_code`/`error_code_for` assertion anywhere in the read-path tests.
ABSENCE: `search_files store_uninitialized` shows the token appears only in a docstring in the test file (line 170), never in an assertion.

Named violating input: if the added `err.error_code = "store_uninitialized"` line is removed, `error_code_for` falls through to `command_failed` (src/rebar/_errors.py:82); all six parametrized reads + show_ticket + parity test stay green (message unchanged), but audit/server would re-raise (500) and the MCP envelope would emit the wrong code — undetected.
advisory.finding: No test asserts the raised error carries error_code == 'store_uninitialized' (nor that error_code_for(exc) returns it) on any read path; every read-path test asserts only the message substring 'not initialized'. The code path's declared contract is the machine-readable code, and audit/server.py branches on it.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_reads_raise_on_absent_store_instead_of_returning_empty (and show_ticket test), add `assert rebar.error_code_for(excinfo.value) == "store_uninitialized"` alongside the message check, pinning the machine-readable contract the audit server and MCP envelope depend on.

evidence: ABSENCE: audit/read.py:154-155 wraps its list_tickets in try/except returning [] so it degrades safely; the four sites above do not, and none is mentioned in the commit's caller sweep
dropped.finding: Several public `rebar.list_tickets` consumers other than the fixed audit-server call site use the `x or []` idiom, which guards against a None/empty return but not against a raised exception; against an uninitialized store they will now raise `RebarError` instead of receiving `[]`. The commit states the caller sweep found only the audit server, but these sites (finalize/sidecar/fp_ledger/artifact_emit) reach the same code through the public API.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the read guard should match the write path's `.git` check (true parity) or document that it deliberately matches the CLI reads' isdir-only condition, since a dir-without-.git store still diverges between reads and writes.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py:101: `if not os.path.isdir(tracker) or not os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, ".git")):`
src/rebar/_reads.py:35: docstring `Read-side mirror of the write path's ``event_prepare._ensure_initialized```
reads_cli.py:340 uses `if not os.path.isdir(tracker):` — so the new guard matches the CLI reads' condition, not the write path's stronger condition
dropped.finding: The new read guard keys only on `os.path.isdir(tracker)`, but the write-path `_ensure_initialized` it claims to mirror also requires `os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, '.git'))`. A tracker directory that exists without a `.git` inside passes the read guard but fails the write guard, so reads and writes still disagree in that case — contradicting the docstring's 'read-side mirror of the write path' / 'same wording the CLI reads and the write path use' parity claim.
